text: kinda sick. imagine a cli that you fuck around in for a bit, put in some parameters or whatever, all built around the library and then it throws down a live server and its there in the browser to check out. idk anything that does that honestly, you could do procedural cities, etc. i mean even to the extent you pass in your own models, they decode into assets, and then are populated from some script someone would setup is wild.
resolution: Captured the CLI/live-browser authoring idea as an SDK implication of the existing ruled architecture: a parameter/script-driven CLI can call the semantic authoring library, import/decode user models into content-addressed assets, bake a gamefile, and serve the browser loader for immediate preview. Noted the boundary: user scripts are authoring/compile-time generators, while runtime behavior still comes from engine capabilities parameterized by data.
